stem: In a shabad of the Guru Granth Sahib, what does the word 'rahao' written after a line mark?
options: the Guru who wrote it, given by number
the raga in which the hymn is to be sung
the refrain, the hymn's central line
the last verse, where the poet signs it
why: Rahao means 'pause' or 'stay': it marks the refrain, the line that holds the shabad's central thought, often sung again between verses. The author is given by Mahala in the heading, and the raga is named above the hymn.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, shabad headings and rahao markings (e.g. Sri Raag, Ang 14)

es.stem: En un shabad del Guru Granth Sahib, ¿qué marca la palabra 'rahao' escrita después de una línea?
options: el Gurú que lo escribió, dado por número
el raga en que debe cantarse el himno
el estribillo, el centro del himno
el último verso, donde firma el poeta
es.why: Rahao significa 'pausa' o 'quédate': marca el estribillo, la línea que guarda la idea central del shabad y que a menudo se vuelve a cantar entre los versos. El autor se indica por Mahala en el encabezado, y el raga se nombra sobre el himno.

stem: Inside each raga section of the Guru Granth Sahib, how are the hymns ordered?
options: the Bhagats' hymns first, then the Gurus' after them
the Gurus' hymns by Mahala, then the Bhagats'
by year of writing, Gurus and Bhagats mixed together
by the first letter of each hymn, in Gurmukhi order
why: Within a raga, the Gurus' compositions come first, arranged by Mahala (Guru Nanak, then the later Gurus), and the hymns of the Bhagats such as Kabir, Namdev and Ravidas follow in the same raga.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, arrangement of the raga sections (e.g. Raag Gauri, Raag Asa)

es.stem: Dentro de cada sección de raga del Guru Granth Sahib, ¿cómo están ordenados los himnos?
options: primero los himnos de los Bhagats, luego los de los Gurús
primero los de los Gurús, por Mahala, luego los Bhagats
por año de escritura, Gurús y Bhagats mezclados
por la primera letra de cada himno, en orden gurmukhi
es.why: Dentro de un raga, primero van las composiciones de los Gurús, ordenadas por Mahala (Guru Nanak y luego los Gurús siguientes), y después siguen, en el mismo raga, los himnos de Bhagats como Kabir, Namdev y Ravidas.

stem: In the Guru Granth Sahib, whose hymns make up the whole of Raag Jaijavanti, the last raga section?
options: Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Guru
Guru Arjan Dev, the fifth Guru
Bhagat Kabir, the weaver of Banaras
Guru Nanak Dev, the first Guru
why: Raag Jaijavanti, the last of the thirty-one ragas, holds only four shabads, all by Guru Tegh Bahadur (Mahala 9). Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1352-1353.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Raag Jaijavanti, Ang 1352-1353

es.stem: En el Guru Granth Sahib, ¿de quién son todos los himnos de Raag Jaijavanti, la última sección de raga?
options: Guru Tegh Bahadur, el noveno Gurú
Guru Arjan Dev, el quinto Gurú
Bhagat Kabir, el tejedor de Benarés
Guru Nanak Dev, el primer Gurú
es.why: Raag Jaijavanti, el último de los treinta y un ragas, tiene solo cuatro shabads, todos de Guru Tegh Bahadur (Mahala 9). Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1352-1353.

stem: A gurdwara is planning kirtan for the coming of spring. Which raga of the Guru Granth Sahib does Sikh tradition sing in that season?
options: Raag Malar
Raag Prabhati
Raag Basant
Raag Sarang
why: Basant means spring, and Sikh tradition sings Raag Basant in the spring season; Malar is the monsoon raga, Prabhati the dawn raga, and Sarang belongs to the heat of midday. Guru Granth Sahib, Raag Basant, Ang 1168.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Raag Basant, Ang 1168

es.stem: Un gurdwara prepara el kirtan para la llegada de la primavera. ¿Qué raga del Guru Granth Sahib canta la tradición sij en esa estación?
options: Raag Malar
Raag Prabhati
Raag Basant
Raag Sarang
es.why: Basant significa primavera, y la tradición sij canta Raag Basant en esa estación; Malar es el raga del monzón, Prabhati el del amanecer y Sarang el del calor del mediodía. Guru Granth Sahib, Raag Basant, Ang 1168.

stem: In the Sidh Gosht (Raag Ramkali), when the yogis urge Guru Nanak to take up their earrings and patched coat, how does he answer?
options: he wears them for a while to honor his hosts
he asks the yogis to answer his questions first
he accepts them as a gift and joins their order
he makes them inner: the Word is the earring
why: Guru Nanak turns the yogi's outward marks inward: the Word (shabad) dwelling within is the true earring, and seeing the One everywhere is the patched coat. Sidh Gosht, Raag Ramkali, Ang 939.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Sidh Gosht, Raag Ramkali, Ang 939

es.stem: En el Sidh Gosht (Raag Ramkali), cuando los yoguis animan a Guru Nanak a llevar sus aretes y su manto de retazos, ¿cómo responde?
options: los usa un tiempo para honrar a sus anfitriones
pide a los yoguis que antes respondan sus preguntas
los acepta como regalo y se une a su orden
los vuelve signos internos: la Palabra es el arete
es.why: Guru Nanak lleva hacia dentro las marcas externas del yogui: la Palabra (shabad) que vive en el interior es el verdadero arete, y ver al Uno en todo es el manto de retazos. Sidh Gosht, Raag Ramkali, Ang 939.

stem: In the Sidh Gosht, Guru Nanak answers the yogis' question about his guru with 'sabad guru, surat dhun chela.' What does this line say?
options: the Word is the Guru; attention to it the disciple
a living sage is the Guru; Nanak is his disciple
the breath is the Guru; holding it still the disciple
the pandit is the Guru; his student is the disciple
why: Asked who his guru is, Guru Nanak answers that the Shabad, the Word, is the Guru, and the attention (surat) attuned to its strain is the disciple. Sidh Gosht, Raag Ramkali, Ang 943.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Sidh Gosht, Raag Ramkali, Ang 943

es.stem: En el Sidh Gosht, Guru Nanak responde a la pregunta de los yoguis sobre su gurú con 'sabad guru, surat dhun chela'. ¿Qué dice esta línea?
options: la Palabra es el Gurú; la atención a ella, el discípulo
un sabio vivo es el Gurú; Nanak es su discípulo
la respiración es el Gurú; retenerla, el discípulo
el pandit es el Gurú; su alumno es el discípulo
es.why: Cuando le preguntan quién es su gurú, Guru Nanak responde que el Shabad, la Palabra, es el Gurú, y que la atención (surat) afinada a su melodía es el discípulo. Sidh Gosht, Raag Ramkali, Ang 943.

stem: What is the Asa di Var in the Guru Granth Sahib, and at what time of day is it customarily sung?
why: The Asa di Var is Guru Nanak's ballad (var) in Raag Asa: twenty-four pauris with saloks by Guru Nanak and Guru Angad set between them. By custom it is sung in kirtan in the gurdwara in the early morning. Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 462-475.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Asa di Var, Ang 462-475

rubric.point: Says it is a var (ballad) in Raag Asa by Guru Nanak, made of stanzas (pauris) with verses (saloks) set between them. Saying only 'a hymn in Raag Asa' counts as partly.
Says it is sung in the early morning, at or before dawn (amrit vela), in gurdwaras. 'Sung every day' with no time of day does not count.
Mentions that some saloks are by Guru Angad, or that it has twenty-four pauris (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: ¿Qué es el Asa di Var en el Guru Granth Sahib, y a qué hora del día se canta por costumbre?
es.why: El Asa di Var es la balada (var) de Guru Nanak en Raag Asa: veinticuatro pauris con saloks de Guru Nanak y Guru Angad intercalados. Por costumbre se canta en el kirtan del gurdwara temprano por la mañana. Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 462-475.

stem: The Mul Mantar calls the One nirbhau and nirvair. What do these two words mean, and how does Guru Tegh Bahadur apply them to the wise person in his saloks near the end of the Guru Granth Sahib?
why: Nirbhau means without fear and nirvair without hate or enmity. In Salok Mahala 9, Guru Tegh Bahadur says the one who frightens no one and fears no one is truly wise. Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1 and Ang 1427.
source: Guru Granth Sahib, Mul Mantar (Ang 1); Salok Mahala 9 (Ang 1427)

rubric.point: Gives nirbhau as without fear and nirvair as without hate or enmity. Getting only one of the two right counts as partly.
Says Guru Tegh Bahadur calls wise the one who frightens no one and fears no one. 'The wise are brave' alone counts as partly.
Notes that the two belong together: fearlessness with no hostility in it (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: El Mul Mantar llama al Uno nirbhau y nirvair. ¿Qué significan estas dos palabras, y cómo las aplica Guru Tegh Bahadur a la persona sabia en sus saloks cerca del final del Guru Granth Sahib?
es.why: Nirbhau significa sin miedo, y nirvair, sin odio ni enemistad. En el Salok Mahala 9, Guru Tegh Bahadur dice que es verdaderamente sabio quien no asusta a nadie ni teme a nadie. Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1 y Ang 1427.
